h1: The 6 Best Microwaves for Apartment Living, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 apartment-friendly microwaves compared on mute buttons, power levels, wattage, defrost options and counter footprint.
summary: The Chefman Compact 0.7 cu. ft. is the best apartment microwave thanks to a mute button, ten power levels, two defrost settings and a child lock. The Toshiba is the pick if you want more cooking power and a larger cavity, the COMFEE' with eleven power levels is the best value for fine control, and the BLACK+DECKER is the plain, safe choice.
intro: Apartment microwaves live a different life from house microwaves. The beep that is merely annoying in a detached kitchen wakes a flatmate through a bedroom wall, the counter is shared between the kettle, the coffee maker and a cutting board, and the outlet is often on a circuit that also feeds the fridge. The spec that matters most is often not wattage at all.

We reviewed six countertop microwaves with those constraints in mind, reading the spec sheets and listings for capacity, power, power level count, defrost options and safety features such as mute and child lock. Features the listings do not state are not assumed, and nothing here relies on a built-in or over-the-range install.

products.name: Chefman Compact Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu. Ft.
products.verdict: A mute button, ten power levels and two defrost modes in a compact 0.7 cu. ft. box.
products.description:
This Chefman is a compact 0.7 cubic foot microwave rated at 700 watts, with ten power levels, two defrost settings, a child safety lock and a mute button. It is aimed squarely at small kitchens.

The mute button is why it wins here. Anyone who has had a shared wall knows the end-of-cycle chime is the part of a microwave you hear most, and silencing it makes late-night cooking possible without a neighbour complaint. Two defrost settings, typically one by weight and one by time, also save you from doing power math with a frozen chicken breast. The tradeoff is the usual 700 watt one: it takes longer than a 900 watt oven on frozen meals.

Buy it if you share walls, cook after midnight or live with a small child who likes buttons. Skip it if you want the fastest possible reheating.
pros: Ten power levels give fine control
products.idealFor: Renters with thin walls and late-night cooking habits.
products.skipIf: You regularly cook frozen meals and want speed.

products.name: TOSHIBA Microwave Oven
products.verdict: 900 watts and 0.9 cu. ft. mean fast meals and room for a real plate.
products.description:
The Toshiba is a 0.9 cubic foot countertop microwave rated at 900 watts. That is the highest output and largest cavity in this ranking, and the listing prices it in the $50 to $100 bracket.

It places second because power and space are what most renters wish their first microwave had. Meals reheat closer to the time on the package, a dinner plate rotates without hitting the walls, and a larger bowl of soup fits without spilling. What it lacks is the thoughtful extras of the Chefman: the listing mentions no mute button, no stated power level count and no dedicated defrost modes.

Choose it if you cook full meals in a one-bedroom and have a free stretch of counter. Skip it if every inch of counter is spoken for or you live in a building where noise is a concern.
products.idealFor: One-bedroom cooks who prepare real meals daily.
products.skipIf: Counter space is limited or noise matters.

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu.Ft
products.verdict: Eleven power levels in a 0.7 cu. ft. cabinet, the finest control in this group.
products.description:
This COMFEE' is a 0.7 cubic foot, 700 watt microwave with eleven power levels. The listing gives few other features, so power-step range is the headline.

It ranks third because eleven steps let you do things most small microwaves handle poorly, such as softening butter, melting chocolate and warming a plate of rice without cooking the edge. Power control matters more in a small kitchen where the microwave does more jobs than an oven you cannot fit. The compromise is everything else: no stated mute, no stated defrost modes and no child lock, so it trails the Chefman for households that need those.

It is a good buy for anyone who cooks gently and wants more than full and half power. Skip it if you need a mute button or lock.
pros: Eleven power levels for gentle cooking
cons: No mute or child lock listed
products.idealFor: Small-kitchen cooks who melt, soften and simmer.
products.skipIf: You need a mute button or child lock.

products.name: Chefman Countertop Microwave Oven 0.7 Cu. Ft.
products.verdict: Ten power levels, eco mode, child lock and mute, but without the Compact's defrost pair.
products.description:
This Chefman is a 0.7 cubic foot, 700 watt microwave that lists ten power levels, eco mode, child lockout and a mute key. It looks very similar to the Compact model above.

It ranks fourth because the Compact version adds two defrost settings, and defrost is a weekly task in a small kitchen. Eco mode is the differentiator here, reducing the energy used while the microwave sits idle, which matters when it is plugged in around the clock and your utilities are part of the rent.

Pick it if you want the Chefman control set and an energy-saving mode. Skip it if you defrost meat often, in which case the Compact is better.
pros: Eco mode trims idle energy use
products.idealFor: Energy-conscious renters who want mute and control.

products.name: COMFEE' Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A dependable 0.7 cu. ft., 700W unit with eco mode that also comes in pearl white.
products.description:
This COMFEE' is a 0.7 cubic foot, 700 watt microwave with an ECO mode. A close sibling is sold in a pearl white finish, which helps in kitchens with white appliances or small, light-coloured rooms.

It sits fifth because it is a solid appliance without any standout feature for apartments. There is no mute button, no stated power level count and no child lock, so it trails the Chefman units. It does match the COMFEE' above on cost and size, and the eco mode gives it a small energy advantage over the plain BLACK+DECKER.

Choose it if you want a mainstream, unfussy microwave and a finish option. Skip it if you want noise control or fine power steps.
pros: Eco mode for idle energy use
products.idealFor: Renters who want a plain eco-aware microwave.
products.skipIf: You live with thin walls or small children.

products.name: BLACK+DECKER Countertop Microwave Oven
products.verdict: A 0.7 cu. ft., 700W microwave with nothing extra and nothing to go wrong.
products.description:
The BLACK+DECKER is a 0.7 cubic foot, 700 watt countertop microwave. The listing offers only capacity and wattage, so treat it as a straightforward heater with standard controls.

It finishes last because the other five add something an apartment cares about: mute, power steps, defrost modes or eco mode. What it does have is a recognised small-appliance name and a footprint that sits in the middle of the market. It is the easy choice for a first apartment, a guest flat or a spare kitchenette where the microwave warms coffee and leftovers.

Buy it if you want the least complicated option. Skip it if you share a wall or want any of the quiet or efficiency features above.
cons: No mute or eco mode listed
products.skipIf: You need quiet operation or fine power steps.

whatMatters.detail: A mute button disables the end-of-cycle beep and the key tones, which is the loudest part of a microwave in a small flat. Without it, a late snack can wake a partner or a neighbour through a thin wall. Look for the word mute on the feature list rather than assuming a volume setting.

A 900W, 0.9 cubic foot oven cooks closer to package times and holds a standard dinner plate. A 700W, 0.7 cubic foot model is smaller and slower, usually needing a third more time on frozen food. Match the wattage to whether you cook from scratch or from the freezer.

More power levels mean more control over gentle tasks like softening butter or warming rice. Ten or eleven levels give far finer steps than the usual half and full. The count appears in the listing title or feature bullets.

Dedicated defrost modes cycle the power so meat thaws without cooking at the edges. Two settings usually mean one by weight and one by time. If the listing does not mention defrost, you will be doing it manually at a low power level.

Eco mode lowers standby draw, which matters if utilities are part of your rent. A 900W microwave pulls more current than a 700W one, and apartment circuits are often shared with other appliances. Check the amperage on the label and avoid sharing the outlet with a toaster or kettle.

faq.q: Will a microwave fit under my cabinets?
faq.a: Check the listing's height and the clearance above your counter, and leave a few inches around the vents. A 0.7 cubic foot model is easier to place than the 0.9 cubic foot Toshiba. Measure twice if your counter sits under a low shelf.

faq.q: What is the biggest mistake renters make with microwaves?
faq.a: Buying the biggest or smallest model without checking the counter, the outlet or the noise. A microwave that does not fit, trips the breaker or beeps loudly is a poor purchase at any price.

faq.q: Is a 900 watt microwave worth it over a 700 watt?
faq.a: If you reheat full plates or cook frozen meals, yes. The Toshiba cooks closer to package time and handles bigger dishes. For coffee, soup and snacks, a 700 watt model performs fine and takes less counter space.

faq.q: How do I set up a microwave in a small kitchen?
faq.a: Place it on a stable, level surface with a few inches of air around the vents, and use a wall outlet instead of an extension cord. Keep it away from the sink and the stove to avoid heat and splashes.

faq.q: How can I keep one clean and odour-free?
faq.a: Heat a bowl of water with a slice of lemon for a few minutes, then wipe the steamed interior with a damp cloth. Cover food while heating to prevent splatter, and wash the turntable by hand.

faq.q: Do I need a mute button?
faq.a: In a studio or a flat with thin walls, it is among the most useful features. Only the two Chefman models list one. If your walls are thick or you live alone, it matters less.

finalTake: The Chefman Compact is the best apartment microwave because it solves the problems renters actually have: noise, small counters and unattended children. Pick the Toshiba when you cook real meals and have the space, the eleven-level COMFEE' for gentle cooking, and the BLACK+DECKER when you just want a basic box. For most shared walls, mute beats extra wattage.
